appearance_facts.fact: Vertical color legend with a white-to-dark-maroon gradient; tick labels 100, 80, 60, 40, 20, 0.
Legend top label '100 Low' (white end) and bottom label '0 High' (dark maroon end), so darker = higher prevalence.
NY polygon filled dark maroon (darkest tier, near 0).
IL polygon filled dark maroon (darkest tier).
KY polygon filled dark maroon (darkest tier).
WA polygon filled dark maroon (darkest tier).
TN polygon filled bright red (high tier, lighter than NY/IL/KY/WA).
TX polygon filled bright red (high tier).

printed_facts.fact: Title: 'Prevalence of Species Z in Each State'.
Scale runs 100 (Low, white) down to 0 (High, dark maroon); no per-state numeric values are printed.
Two-letter codes printed inside polygons, e.g. NY (x~1340,y~490), IL (x~1200,y~750), KY (x~1450,y~810), WA (x~250,y~270), NC (x~1590,y~840), DE (x~1620,y~680).
NC filled pale yellow/cream (low tier, near 80-100 on the scale).

public_definitions: Routing criterion: 'Highest prevalence state in the dashboard'.
uncertain: No numeric prevalence value is printed for any state; ranking relies solely on color shading, so exact ordering among the darkest states (NY, IL, KY, WA) cannot be confirmed from the image.
NY, IL, KY, and WA all appear in the same darkest maroon tier; the dashboard does not provide a tie-breaker to confirm NY as strictly the single highest.
